process.title: Initial Consultation
process.text: We discuss your products, export goals and target customers in Germany, and confirm whether DVGW certification is the right route.

process.title: Feasibility Assessment
process.text: We identify the applicable DVGW rules, EN standards and hygiene requirements, and estimate effort, cost and timeline.

process.title: Documentation Review
process.text: Our engineers review your drawings, material declarations, quality records and test reports against certification-body expectations.

process.title: Gap Analysis
process.text: We compare your product and factory against every requirement and produce a prioritised action plan to close the gaps.

process.title: Testing Preparation
process.text: We define the test programme, select representative samples, run pre-tests and prepare the test application.

process.title: Laboratory Testing
process.text: Accredited laboratories in Germany or Europe carry out type testing. We coordinate samples, shipping, queries and re-tests.

process.title: Factory Audit
process.text: The certification body inspects your factory production control. We prepare your team with mock audits and on-site support.

process.title: Certification Submission
process.text: We compile the complete certification file and submit it to the certification body, then manage all clarifications.

process.title: Approval
process.text: The certification body evaluates the results and issues the certificate and registration number.

process.title: German Market Entry
process.text: We support your launch in Germany: technical sales documents, distributor introductions, tenders and surveillance audits.

faqs.a: DVGW (Deutscher Verein des Gas- und Wasserfaches e.V.) is the German technical and scientific association that sets the rules for the drinking-water sector. Founded in 1859, it publishes the technical rules German water utilities follow. Through its certification body, DVGW CERT GmbH, it certifies products, companies and specialists against these rules and the related European standards.

faqs.q: Is DVGW certification mandatory in Germany?
faqs.a: For many drinking-water products, DVGW certification is not legally required in every case. In practice, however, German utilities, installers, wholesalers and public tenders expect it as proof of conformity with the generally accepted rules of technology. For products in contact with drinking water, the German Drinking Water Ordinance also requires materials to meet the hygiene criteria of the German Environment Agency (UBA), and certification is the usual way to demonstrate this.

Manufacturers of products used in German drinking-water systems: valves, pipes, fittings, pumps, water meters, water treatment equipment and their components. Indian manufacturers who want to sell to German utilities, distributors or OEMs usually need it to be considered at all.

Products used in water supply and in building installations, including valves, pipes, fittings and connectors, pumps, water meters, filters and softeners, and backflow preventers. Our Certification Knowledge Center lists typical requirements for each category.

Typically 6 to 12 months from application to certificate. Simple products with complete documentation can be faster. Products that need long-term tests, such as plastic pipes, or new materials take longer. Good preparation is the biggest factor you can control.

faqs.q: What does the certification process involve?
faqs.a: Application and document review, type testing of samples at an accredited laboratory, an initial inspection of your factory production control, evaluation by the certification body and issue of the certificate. After that, regular surveillance audits keep the certificate valid.

faqs.q: How long is a DVGW certificate valid?
faqs.a: Certificates are issued for a limited period, commonly up to five years, subject to the certification body's conditions and successful surveillance. Changes to the product, materials or production site must be reported and may require additional testing.

Typically: company registration, product datasheets, technical drawings, material specifications, quality certificates (for example ISO 9001), existing test reports, manufacturing process documentation, product images, inspection records and factory information. The Product Certification Requirements page has a checklist for each product category.

faqs.q: Do documents have to be in German?
faqs.a: Many certification bodies accept technical documents in English. Product marking, installation instructions and user information for the German market are usually expected in German. ESC coordinates professional technical translation where needed.

Costs depend on the product range, the number of test samples, the scope of laboratory testing, travel for the factory audit and annual surveillance fees. Laboratory and certification-body fees are charged directly by those bodies. After a short feasibility assessment, ESC gives you a transparent estimate before any commitment.

Yes. Good grouping of product variants, using materials that already hold approvals, complete documentation and in-house pre-testing all reduce laboratory costs and failed tests. Most of our preparation work is aimed at avoiding expensive re-tests.

ESC acts as your intermediary and project manager. We interpret the requirements, prepare and review documentation, close gaps, coordinate laboratories and the certification body in German, prepare your factory for audits and support your entry into the German market.

No. ESC is an independent consulting and coordination partner. Certificates are issued only by the certification body, for example DVGW CERT GmbH. This independence lets us represent your interests throughout the process.

faqs.q: Do you support markets beyond Germany?
faqs.a: Yes. DVGW certification is widely recognised in Austria, Switzerland and other European markets, and many requirements overlap with European standards. We can advise on related schemes and on combined certification strategies for the EU.
